input: In today's fast-paced manufacturing environment, improving product quality remains a crucial priority, and defect reduction plays a pivotal role in enhancing overall operational efficiency. This report delves into a recent defect-reduction project undertaken on a moulding cell and showcases the results that were achieved over the course of one quarter. At the beginning of the quarter, the reject rate stood at 4.6%, which meant that a significant share of the units produced by the cell were being rejected. By the end of the quarter, thanks to the efforts of the project team, this figure had been brought down to 3.1%, representing a reduction of 1.5 percentage points and highlighting the effectiveness of the measures that were implemented. When this improvement is viewed in the context of the cell's annual production volume of 138k units per year, its impact becomes even more tangible: the reduction of 1.5 percentage points corresponds to approximately 2070 fewer rejected units each year (138k x 0.015), underscoring meaningful savings in materials, rework, and disposal efforts. It is important to note, however, that the quarter in question also included a planned shutdown, and the reported rates have not been adjusted for this shutdown, so a degree of caution is warranted when interpreting the results. Overall, the project delivered a robust improvement in quality performance, cutting the reject rate from 4.6% to 3.1% and avoiding about 2070 rejected units per year at the stated volume of 138k units per year.
target: A defect-reduction project on a moulding cell reduced the reject rate from 4.6% to 3.1% over one quarter. The reject rate is the share of produced units that are rejected, so the change is a reduction of 1.5 percentage points in that share, measured on the same cell before and after the project. At the stated volume of 138k units per year, a reduction of 1.5 percentage points corresponds to about 2070 fewer rejected units per year (138k x 0.015). The annual figure is a projection from the quarterly rates: it holds the rates and the volume fixed, and it inherits the uncertainty of both. The quarter included a planned shutdown, and the reported rates are not adjusted for the shutdown. The comparison therefore mixes production in normal running with production around a stopped period, and the reported figures do not separate a project effect from any shutdown effect on the rates. The size of a shutdown effect is not stated. Within that limit, the recorded outcome stands as follows: a reject rate of 3.1% against 4.6% before the project, and an implied avoidance of about 2070 rejected units per year at a volume of 138k units per year.
